summary: Unexpected OPTIONS (CORS preflight) requests being counted toward per-route quota on dedicated multiplexer causing opaque 429s
description:
Issue summary:
BeaconDocs reported a spike of opaque 429 responses for a real-time and batch-mix workload on their Dedicated pool. Root cause traced to CORS preflight (OPTIONS) requests and some health-probe traffic being routed through the multiplexer/route layer and counted against per-route quotas. The ingress edge was rewriting paths and normalizing OPTIONS onto the same route key as POST/GET, which made the rate-limiter attribute preflight to the interactive route token pool.

Impact:
- Customer saw ~15% of interactive chat requests receive 429s intermittently for 2 regions (primarily eu-west) during peak batch import windows.
- Affected core feature: chat responses and webhook callbacks delayed; no data loss but increased latency and client retries.
- Billing unaffected, but customer SLA risk and business impact (support tickets, user-facing errors).

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated GPU pool (customer BeaconDocs, dedicated tier)
- Region: eu-west (primary), occasional cross-region fallover to us-east during testing
- Traffic pattern: mixed long-lived WebSocket/HTTP2 connections for chat + parallel bulk embedding POSTs; fronted by customer-managed edge (combined with Redwood ingress).
- Observed with HTTP/2 keep-alive and connection multiplexing enabled on customer proxy.

Steps to reproduce (customer test case):
1) Configure a small dedicated pool and pin route /v1/chat to a priority lane.
2) From a client behind an HTTP/2-capable proxy, open several long-lived streams and start sending chat messages.
3) Simultaneously run a bulk embedding job that issues many POST requests and triggers CORS preflight from a browser-like agent (OPTIONS).
4) Observe that the ingress logs show OPTIONS mapped to the same route key as POST and counted against the route's quota leading to 429s on subsequent chat POSTs.

Logs & artifacts attached by customer (redacted):
- Sample ingress request lines: 
  [2026-03-08T15:12:03Z] "OPTIONS /v1/embed/batch HTTP/2" 200 route_key=route:/v1/embed/batch mapped_route=/v1/chat
  [2026-03-08T15:12:04Z] "POST /v1/chat HTTP/2" 429 route_key=route:/v1/chat
- Snapshot of rate-limiter counters at time of spike (trimmed): preflight_count=512, route_token_window=0, refill_last=2026-03-08T15:10:00Z
- Customer-provided pcap showing repeated OPTIONS from browser workers in parallel with chat streams.

Requested outcome from customer:
- Clarify why OPTIONS are being counted and how to prevent preflight traffic from consuming route-level tokens.
- Short-term workaround to stop immediate 429s while engineering deploys a permanent fix.
comments: 2026-03-08 | Aisha Patel (Support): Received initial report and logs from BeaconDocs. Opening ticket and escalating to SRE. Marked as P1 due to customer SLA risk.
2026-03-08 | Marco Nguyen (On-call SRE): Acknowledged. Asked for sample ingress access logs and asked BeaconDocs to pause batch preflight generators for immediate mitigation.
2026-03-08 | BeaconDocs (Customer): Confirmed can pause the browser-based bulk importer for 30 mins; provided ingress logs and pcap. Reported reduction in 429s during pause window.

2026-03-09 | Marco Nguyen (SRE): Initial hypothesis: ingress rewrite rule is normalizing OPTIONS to canonical route, falling through to route-level accounting. Creating quick passthrough config for OPTIONS and health probes as temporary mitigation.
2026-03-10 | Eng (Ingress team): Deployed config change to ignore OPTIONS at the edge and not emit route_key for method OPTIONS. Observed drop in preflight_count and 429s almost eliminated.
2026-03-11 | Marco Nguyen (SRE): Patch merged to main ingress repo to explicitly filter out OPTIONS and known probe user-agents from per-route quota; customer confirmed resolution. Closing ticket.
investigation_notes: Ingress rewrite rules: customer edge was rewriting incoming path prefixes; our ingress then ran path normalization which combined method-agnostic keys leading to preflight attribution to interactive route.

Rate-limiter behavior: per-route token accounting keyed by (normalized_path, priority_lane). The normalization step ignored HTTP method when preflight requests were presented and therefore counted OPTIONS same as POST for the same normalized path.

Multiplexing impact: HTTP/2 connection reuse from the customer proxy led to OPTIONS from a different logical client being attributed to the same API key/route bucket due to edge connection pooling and mis-mapped route_key header.
Repro scripts: created a lightweight repro (curl + http2 push) to exercise OPTIONS and then POST; reproduced locally against a staging ingress build.
resolution: Short-term: Applied ingress config to drop/ignore OPTIONS (CORS preflight) and known healthcheck user-agents from per-route accounting for the customer's dedicated pool. Also advised BeaconDocs to enable CORS preflight caching (Access-Control-Max-Age) and reduce browser preflight frequency.\nPermanent: Merged code change that makes route_key include HTTP method for ambiguity-prone paths OR explicitly excludes OPTIONS from route-level token accounting. Deployed to staging and rolled to prod for dedicated pools in eu-west on 2026-03-10.\nFollow-up actions: Update runbook to include preflight exclusion test and add a console dashboard that surfaces preflight-to-post ratios per route (ticketed: INT-4450). Customer confirmed that errors ceased after the deployment and resumed bulk jobs successfully.
